1000449.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Portuguese Moçambique (“Mozambique”). The Portuguese name was first applied to the Island of Mozambique and its settlement and was later extended to the surrounding colonial territory and ultimately to the modern country. The island's name is generally traced to a local Arab ruler encountered by the Portuguese in the late 15th century, whose name is recorded in varying forms such as Ali Musa Mbiki, Mussa Ben-Bique and Mussa Al-Mbique.
The identifiable given-name element مُوسَى (mūsā, “Moses; Musa”) is from Classical Syriac ܡܘܼܫܹܐ (“Moses”), from Biblical Hebrew מֹשֶׁ
